item.title: A Steady Theory for Highly Unsteady Thin Airfoil Motions
item.description: arXiv:2611.30074v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A generalized steady thin airfoil theory is built not from steady flow, but from flows in which there exists a frame of reference where the absolute vorticity field is steady. We specialize this general idea to construct a foliation of a domain of phase space for thin airfoil motions in which staying on a leaf of the foliation maintains zero absolute vorticity in the fluid indefinitely. The phase space is described by the airfoil's total rotation rate, speed, and angle of attack. It is found using this definition that one of the preeminent unsteady stall conditions is equivalent to the traditional steady stall condition for this class of flows, various other classical results can be re-interpreted as steady in the absolute vorticity field, and insight is also provided into the surprising experimental results of McGowan et al. (AIAA J. 49, 2011). We show parts of existing quasi-steady flow and Theodorsen unsteady flow theory can be built from a planar approximation of our foliation, making the quasi-steady extension of our theory trivial, and suggesting how an unsteady extension can be created as well. Furthermore, pure unsteady effects in the new theory amount to a transversal of the leaves, occupying just one dimension, inviting interesting prospects for future experimental and theoretical work.
item.dc:creator: Scott A. Bollt

item.title: Diffusivity and metric exponents for slightly supercritical percolation in high dimensions
item.dc:creator: Chenlin Gu, Tom Hutchcroft, Xiaoran Li

item.title: A note on Kaluza-Klein theories
item.description: arXiv:2611.30285v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present a variant of the Kaluza-Klein theory that was introduced in previous papers (ATMP, 2020; LMP 2022; Ann. Fac. Sci. Toulouse, 2025), based on an action functional whose critical points, in the presence of point-wise constraints, lead-under reasonable assumptions-to the existence of a principal fiber bundle and solutions to the Einstein-Yang-Mills system. The difference is that it is not necessary to impose a point-wise constraint.
item.dc:creator: Fr{\'e}d{\'e}ric H{\'e}lein (IMJ-PRG)

item.title: Darboux transformation for the ASDYM equations: Solitons and instantons
item.description: arXiv:2611.30433v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Using a one-fold Darboux transformation for the anti-self-dual Yang--Mills equations, we express the Yang--Mills Lagrangian density in terms of $\tau$-functions. For solitons constructed from exponential functions, we show that the associated $\tau$-functions admit a parametrization by arbitrary points in the Grassmannian Gr(N,M;$\mathbb{C}$), and construct the corresponding Yang--Mills fields. For instantons arising from the Atiyah--Drinfeld--Hitchin--Manin (ADHM) construction, we reinterpret the ADHM construction in terms of a one-fold Darboux transformation, recover Osborn's formula for the Yang--Mills Lagrangian density, and obtain the corresponding gauge connection.
item.dc:creator: Shangshuai Li

item.title: Virasoro operators for relative Gromov--Witten theory
item.description: arXiv:2611.30566v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $D$ be a smooth divisor in a smooth projective variety $X$. We construct relative Virasoro operators acting on the relative descendant potential of $(X,D)$. Each operator is the logarithmic Virasoro operator of $(X,D)$ plus a boundary correction determined only by $D$ and its normal bundle in $X$. Assuming the Virasoro conjecture for $D$, we prove that the relative constraints are equivalent to the absolute constraints for $X$. Under the same assumption, we establish compatibility with the degeneration formula for two-component projective semistable degenerations satisfying a completeness condition. Consequently, the Virasoro conjecture for the two components and the gluing divisor implies the conjecture for the general fiber. As an application, we prove the Virasoro conjecture for Enriques surfaces in every integral curve class.
item.dc:creator: Shuai Guo, Longting Wu, Lei You

item.title: Geometry of ground states in the long-range Ising model
item.description: arXiv:2611.30604v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the ground states of the ferromagnetic Ising model on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ with long-range interactions and prescribed exterior data. We first show that the half-space configuration is a ground state, by means of a discrete calibration (which is the lattice counterpart of the calibrations of Cabr\'e and Pagliari for nonlocal minimal surfaces). In dimension $d\ge2$ and for positive kernels, the half-space configuration is the unique minimizer in every finite domain, and it is "stable" with respect to perturbations of the exterior datum whose energy is below half of a positive excitation gap. This rigidity has no counterpart in the continuum. For general exterior data and positive kernels, we show that along a monotone family the minimizer is unique except for finitely many data. This can be considered a "generic uniqueness result" that provides the discrete counterpart of a recent work of Dipierro, Fern\'andez-Real and Valdinoci in the continuum. We then introduce a pointwise notion, called perception, which is the lattice counterpart of the instability and stickiness phenomena for nonlocal minimal surfaces discovered by Dipierro, Savin and Valdinoci. We give a local criterion for the half-space configuration to be perceptive at a given site. Finally, we consider a box with exterior datum $+1$ above and below a slab and $-1$ on its sides. For fractional kernels with small exponent, the minimizer is $+1$ in the whole box, and its positive phase is connected. For short-range kernels, instead, the negative phase may enter the box, and the positive phase may be disconnected. Moreover, if the datum is $-1$ around the box and $+1$ only at distance two from it, the configuration identically $-1$ is perceptive at every boundary site of the box for fractional kernels with small exponent.
item.dc:creator: Serena Dipierro, Riccardo Sabbatini, Enrico Valdinoci

item.title: Quantifying superposition via coherence by stochastic orthogonalization
item.description: arXiv:2611.30656v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Here we present an approach to quantifying superposition of nonorthogonal reference states through quantum coherence. No change of basis achieves this: every orthonormal basis makes some superposition-free states appear coherent. We show that orthogonalization succeeds instead as a measurement mapping every reference state onto a multiple of a basis vector in each outcome; such measurements are exactly the free operations that convert superposition into coherence. The largest average coherence they extract from a state, which we call its degree of superposition, turns every coherence measure into a superposition measure with the same operational meaning. An interference term becomes coherence at most with the probability of unambiguously discriminating its two reference states, a bound attained when there are no others and, for positive coefficients and nonnegative overlaps, exactly when the overlaps are probabilities of a random grouping. Maximal degree means conversion into a maximally coherent state with certainty, possible for up to three reference states but not in general. Each coherence measure gives its own degree; when two degrees order two superpositions oppositely, neither converts into the other with certainty, and we find such pairs already for two reference states, unlike in qubit coherence. For equal positive overlaps, in-phase superpositions are rigid: deterministic conversions that keep all components can only permute their coefficients. As the reference states merge, the degree stays bounded where widely used measures can diverge, and at every amplitude a rotation-symmetric cat state attains its maximum. Our results quantify superposition operationally and reveal conversion constraints created by nonorthogonality.
item.dc:creator: G\"okhan Torun

item.title: Computational Complexity and Energy Landscapes of Coulomb Crystals
item.description: arXiv:2611.30657v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Simulated annealing is widely used to search for ground states of trapped-ion Coulomb crystals and of charges on a sphere (the Thomson problem). Elementary nonuniform bounds clarify the role of the input encoding. For identical ions in a fixed trap, unary ion count and a binary energy threshold define a decision problem in P/poly; NP-hardness would imply a collapse of the polynomial hierarchy. The same holds on the unit sphere. With unary ion count and logarithmic precision parameter, approximate configuration search on the sphere and in a fixed positive-definite harmonic trap admits a solution function in FP/poly. These advice bounds provide no uniform search algorithm. In simulations of up to 100 ions, the number of distinct minima found and the time to reach the best-known minimum both grow approximately exponentially. When ions are pinned to prescribed candidate sites, choosing which sites to occupy to minimize the Coulomb energy is NP-hard in two and three dimensions; a finite-precision promise version is NP-complete. All ions are identical, the interaction is bare Coulomb repulsion, and the hardness is carried by the site positions alone. We extend a previous inverse-square reduction to the Coulomb interaction by deriving its angular law, including the quartic field term, and sharpening two estimates. The construction is an array of quadrupoles whose common monopole term cancels from energy differences between legal configurations. Its energy landscapes exhibit large barriers between nearly degenerate minima. Barrier trees resolve this structure, and simulated annealing becomes trapped above the ground state in the cube example. At laboratory parameters, with individually tunable well depths, the encoding survives numerically on a half-filled square lattice. For Doppler-cooled strontium ions, this requires stiff wells a few to tens of micrometers apart, as in electrode trap arrays.
item.dc:creator: Paco Navarro, Michael Emmerich

item.title: Modeling and analysis of a phase-field model for organic solar cells
item.description: arXiv:2611.30660v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We derive and analyze a phase-field model describing the formation of the active layer of organic solar cells. The process combines phase separation of an electron donor (polymer) and an electron acceptor (non-fullerene acceptor) with evaporation of a solvent. Taking the macroscopic motion of the fluid into account, this results in a coupled system of incompressible Navier--Stokes, degenerate multispecies Cahn--Hilliard, and Allen--Cahn equations with cross-diffusion terms. We give a thermodynamically consistent derivation of the system and prove the existence of global-in-time weak solutions without any size constraints on the data. The solutions dissipate the total energy and require an ad-hoc variational formulation of the definition of the diffusion fluxes, which is made necessary by the degeneracy of the mobility matrix.
item.dc:creator: Jan-Frederik Pietschmann, Carmen Tretmans, Nicola Zamponi

item.title: Bifurcation Structure and Coexisting Dynamical States in Two Inductively Coupled Josephson Junctions
item.description: arXiv:2611.30724v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Inductively coupled Josephson junctions support coexisting stationary and running states whose selection depends on both circuit parameters and initial conditions. We investigate the model of a direct current-driven resistively and capacitively shunted junction pair as coupled nonlinear oscillators at zero external magnetic flux, allowing unequal bias, damping and inductive coupling parameters. Equilibrium equations, nullclines, and Jacobian spectra are combined with multiple-initial-condition simulations, finite-time Lyapunov spectra, and Poincar\'e returns to characterize changes in the system dynamics under varying initial conditions and parameter settings. The fixed-point bifurcation diagrams reveal the creation, destruction or annihilation of equilibria and non-monotonic changes in their number under asymmetric coupling. In representative asymmetric parameter slices, nondegenerate saddle-node bifurcations generate or terminate stable equilibria within intervals that also support periodic or chaotic running motion. The running dynamics exhibit period-doubling, period-cascading sequences and embedded periodic windows within chaotic regions, while the initial-condition scans resolve their coexistence with stationary states. These results connect the local equilibrium structure with the parameter-dependent organization and selection of dynamical regimes in the coupled-junction system.
item.dc:creator: Ruijie He, Shenglan Yuan

item.title: Free energy of the bipartite random assignment problem
item.description: arXiv:2611.30801v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We compute the limiting free energy of the bipartite random assignment problem for every pseudodimension $d>0$ and every inverse temperature $\lambda > 0$ at the scale $n^{1/d}$. We show that the limit is given by a rigorous replica-symmetric formula determined by the unique solution of a recursive distributional equation on a Poisson-weighted infinite tree, confirming conjectures of Aldous and Talagrand. As a consequence, for a fixed inverse temperature $\lambda > 0$, we deduce exponential concentration of the cost of a Gibbs assignment and determine the exponential growth rate of the number of near-optimal assignments.
item.dc:creator: Jacob Shkrob

item.title: A particle method for the space homogeneous Lenard-Balescu equation
item.description: arXiv:2611.30808v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We propose a structure preserving particle method to numerically approximate the spatially homogeneous Lenard-Balescu equation for collisional plasmas. The Lenard-Balescu operator is an improvement of the Landau equation with a dielectric function taking the dynamic screening effect into account. Our particle method is based on the variational formulation of the Lenard-Balescu equation under suitable regularization analogous to the strategy followed for the Landau collision operator in [12]. The method guarantees the conservation laws and the entropy dissipation at the semi-discrete level. The novel difficulty of the nonlocal nonlinear dependence of the dielectric function is tackled by rewriting it as integrals in terms of orthogonal and parallel components to the frequency variable. This equivalent form reduces the evaluation of the dielectric function to numerically computing an integral of the directional derivative of the solution on a hyperplane orthogonal to the frequency variable and its one-dimensional Hilbert transform. An efficient implementation of the numerical approximation for the Lenard-Balescu kernel is derived by exploiting this expression of the dielectric function. We finally validate our method by means of several numerical tests, further allowing us to explore qualitative properties of the Lenard-Balescu equation.
item.dc:creator: Jos\'e Antonio Carrillo, Timon Gutleb, Andrea Medaglia, Yijia Tang

item.title: Exponential advantage in quantum observation with one extra qubit
item.description: arXiv:2611.30876v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: While quantum technologies promise to revolutionise how we observe the physical world, achieving substantial advantages with minimal overhead remains a central pursuit. Here, we show that augmenting a quantum machine with just one extra qubit yields an exponential advantage in probing quantum many-body dynamics. We propose an algorithm that uses this qubit to coherently interfere dynamical trajectories, simultaneously estimating exponentially many multi-time correlators with exponentially fewer evolutions than any ancilla-free scheme. Remarkably, this advantage holds even when the ancilla-free machine has unrestricted coherence time and arbitrary adaptive control, and persists even for a single correlator. We further prove that extending coherence time exponentially enhances observational power, establishing our protocol's optimality in both space and time. Finally, we numerically demonstrate our approach by predicting higher-order probe signals in a many-body system with orders-of-magnitude fewer experimental runs than previous methods. These results highlight the broad utility of our framework across quantum learning, sensing, and simulation.
item.dc:creator: Zhenyu Du, Xiongfeng Ma, Vlatko Vedral, Jinzhao Sun

item.title: Wigner Matrices and the $\alpha$-Determinant
item.description: arXiv:2611.30883v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For a Hermitian Wigner matrix $M_n$ and complex $\alpha$ with $|\alpha|\leq1$, we study the $\alpha$-characteristic polynomial $\det_\alpha(zI-M_n)$, which interpolates between the characteristic polynomial ($\alpha=-1$) and the permanental polynomial ($\alpha=1$). Assuming finite fourth moments off the diagonal and second moments on it, we show that this polynomial, normalized by its expectation, converges in distribution off the segment $\sqrt{-\alpha}\,[-2,2]$ to the Wick exponential of an explicit Gaussian analytic function, with the same Gaussian modes for every $\alpha$. As consequences, all zeros lie near this segment with probability tending to one, the empirical zero measure converges to a rotated semicircle law, and analytic linear statistics of the zeros satisfy a central limit theorem. We also show that $\det_\alpha(zI-M_n)$ is approximated, with vanishing relative error, in terms of the characteristic polynomial of $M_n$ at a transformed point. The proof writes the $\alpha$-characteristic polynomial as a polymer gas, which becomes asymptotically ideal after an exact resummation over matchings.
item.dc:creator: Frederic Koehler, Pui Kuen Leung

item.title: On the Finite-Time Singularities of Point-Vortex Systems II: Upper Right Quadrant
item.description: arXiv:2611.30946v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study finite-time singularities of point-vortex systems in the upper right quadrant. For two vortices with arbitrary nonzero circulations and distinct initial positions, we prove global existence and uniqueness by excluding interior collisions, boundary approach, and finite-time escape to infinity. For three vortices with arbitrary nonzero circulations, we rule out finite-time boundary approach in the limit inferior sense, without assuming boundedness or convergence of the trajectories. The argument combines Hamiltonian estimates, monotonicity of signed coordinate moments, and geometric estimates adapted to both walls and the corner. We also establish the existence of finite-time interior collapse for every nonzero circulation triple whose pairwise products sum to zero. The collapse point can be prescribed arbitrarily in the interior, with any sufficiently small positive collapse time. The resulting solutions are asymptotically self-similar, exhibiting square-root contraction and logarithmic rotation. They are constructed using a local strong stable manifold of real dimension two in a similarity system augmented by a complex scale.
item.dc:creator: Cheng Yang

item.title: Gradient formula from the sphere for perturbative RG flows near critical dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2611.31050v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the gradient property of perturbative renormalisation group flows in $d=d_c-\varepsilon$, with a potential and a metric regular at $\varepsilon=0$ up to logarithms of gauge couplings. We state properties of the renormalised functional with local couplings on the sphere $S^d$: finiteness, a local Weyl anomaly, the Ward identity of a conformal Killing vector, rotation properties and statements on the free theory. From them we derive a Ward identity without anomaly for a combination of the functional and its anomaly. Its first variation is a gradient formula whose symmetric metric contains the two-point function on the sphere and whose potential at fixed points is, in an extended form of the properties, proportional to the sphere free energy $\tilde F$ up to a constant. Sources of relevant operators enter through their Weyl variation, and in a scheme which we construct the gradient formula persists, with a nondegenerate metric if a matrix of the free theory is invertible. For multiscalar $\phi^4$ theory and for scalars and Dirac fermions with Yukawa and quartic couplings in $d=4-\varepsilon$, for sextic scalars in $d=3-\varepsilon$ and for cubic scalars in $d=6-\varepsilon$, we derive all these properties from a finiteness hypothesis. The gradient formula then holds to all orders for the beta function defined on the sphere. For interacting gauge theories the properties remain assumptions.
item.dc:creator: Marten Reehorst

item.title: A Quantum Model from the Riemann-Siegel Formula
item.description: arXiv:2611.31116v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct a two-component quantum model in which destructive interference selects the critical-line zeros of a regularized zeta function within a continuous spectrum. Starting from the exact Riemann--Siegel integral representation, we define $\zeta_{\rm reg}(s)$ by subtracting the contribution of the pole at the origin. The two remaining contour integrals supply the interfering amplitudes. A Dirichlet heat filter suppresses high spatial frequencies, and an arithmetic dressing has a profile generated by prime-power dilations. These transformations map the dilation generator to a self-adjoint, parity--time ($PT$) symmetric Hamiltonian on a physical Hilbert space with a positive metric. Its spectrum is real and continuous. The computed lower critical-line zeros of $\zeta_{\rm reg}(s)$ lie close to the corresponding Riemann zeros and exhibit spacing and pair-correlation statistics consistent with the Gaussian unitary ensemble over the sampled range. Whether every analytic zero in the lower half of the critical strip belongs to the physical spectral family remains open.
item.dc:creator: Germ\'an Sierra

item.title: A strict Neumann-Dirichlet eigenvalue inequality on planar domains
item.description: arXiv:2611.31134v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: On simply connected, bounded planar Lipschitz domains it is known from our earlier work that the ($k+2$)-nd eigenvalue of the Neumann Laplacian cannot exceed the $k$-th Dirichlet eigenvalue. In this note we sharpen this statement by showing that this inequality is always strict. This was previously only known under additional assumptions.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Rohleder

item.title: Polynomial mixing for 2D Ising with plus boundary conditions
item.description: arXiv:2611.31180v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the Glauber dynamics of the 2D Ising model at low temperatures. In the absence of boundary conditions, the mixing time on an $n\times n$ box is exponential in $n$ due to a bottleneck between metastable plus and minus phases. When the symmetry is broken via all-plus boundary conditions, it has been predicted in the physics literature since work of Lifshitz (1962) that from an all-minus initialization, the minus droplet shrinks via mean-curvature flow on timescales that are quadratic in $n$, and thus, the system equilibrates in polynomial time. On the rigorous side, the strongest result was a quasi-polynomial mixing time upper bound due to Lubetzky, Martinelli, Sly and Toninelli (2013); a proof of polynomial mixing remained one of the major challenges in the field. We prove this polynomial mixing time bound at all low temperatures. The key step is to establish fast mixing of the interface separating the plus and minus phases on a box with Dobrushin boundary conditions. In simpler models of height functions, polynomial bounds tend to rely on exact harmonic properties and connections to a discrete heat equation. However, the Ising interface exhibits microscopic defects that necessitate the development of a more robust method. We address this via a new multiscale approach to bound mixing times of general disordered random-walk bridges that homogenize to a Brownian bridge at mesoscopic scales. Another notable ingredient is a novel application of censoring to reduce the mixing time problem to proving only a weak Poincar\'e inequality, or warm-start mixing bound, allowing us to assume suitable regularity conditions on the interface and bubbles.
item.dc:creator: Shirshendu Ganguly, Reza Gheissari

item.title: Tensionless M5-brane in light-cone gauge. The spinor moving frame method is wanted
item.description: arXiv:2611.31189v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We perform the complete light-cone gauge fixing for the tensionless limit of the M-theory 5-brane the action for which was recently obtained in [1]. The problem of gauge fixing of local fermionic $\kappa$-symmetry becomes quite nontrivial because the projector of that is constructed from the gauge field strength which in its turn is required to be nonvanaishing and nontrivial in this limit. To resolve this problem the spinor moving frame method has been adapted. The corresponding moving frame is constructed on a vector quadratic in the gauge field strength, which is required to be nonvanishing and nondegenerate in the tensionless limit, and the derivative of the PST (Pasti-Sorokin-Tonin) scalar. The symmetries of the gauge fixed action and equations of motion are briefly discussed. To make a comparison with the case of usual tensionless p-branes (null-p-branes), those which do not carry worldvolume gauge fields, we also elaborate their spinor moving frame formulation.
item.dc:creator: Igor Bandos

item.title: Advancing the Theory of Pretty Good Quantum Operations
item.description: arXiv:2611.31207v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Finding optimal quantum measurements or recovery maps is often demanding. Pretty good measurements and Petz maps offer explicit approximations achieving at least the square of optimal performance by the Barnum-Knill bound. We unify these operations in a semidefinite programming framework with a tunable power, extending them to broader quantum tasks. We prove a stronger bound for powers above one up to three that peaks at quadratic power. For structured channels such as stabilizer codes under Pauli noise, large powers steer recovery to a maximum likelihood decoder for maximally mixed inputs.
item.dc:creator: Bikun Li, Guo Zheng, Liang Jiang

item.title: Analytical solution of general interface problems for reaction-advection-diffusion equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.31226v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We obtain novel integral representations, expressed as contour integrals in the complex Fourier plane, for the solution of fully nonhomogeneous interface problems for classical reaction-advection-diffusion (RAD) equations with arbitrary initial data on the line and general interface conditions at the origin. Such problems of applied mathematics emerge in a spectacular variety of physical phenomena in mathematical physics, chemistry, continuum mechanics, biology, pharmacokinetics, as well as mathematical finance. A suitable implementation of Fokas' unified transform method is in force herein, with particular challenges arising due to inclusion in the model of lower-order terms, and the generality of interface problems under consideration. To our knowledge, this careful analysis has not appeared in (nor does it follow easily from) literature published so far. Our explicit formulae directly lend themselves to explorations of solutions' qualitative properties such as regularity, asymptotic behavior and well-posedness. This work has also been of utility in the investigation of nonlinear counterparts as well as in the study of phase-transition phenomena, moving-interface and diffuse-interface problems. Such results for RAD and high-order PDEs will soon appear in a series of separate papers.
item.dc:creator: Andreas Chatziafratis, Guenbo Hwang, Georgia Karali

item.title: General Slit Stochastic L\"owner Evolution and Conformal Field Theory
item.description: arXiv:1510.04123v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This monograph is dedicated to a generalization of the L\"owner equation in its stochastic form, known as SLE, and to its coupling with the Gaussian free field, with the ultimate aim of constructing a boundary conformal field theory with one free scalar bosonic field. The exposition aims to be a systematic, and hopefully concise, account and generalization of known elements of the theory of L\"owner evolution. We also study the relation to singular representations of the Virasoro algebra, as well as methods of numerical simulation. The main results are proofs of the basic properties of the generalized SLE and general necessary and sufficient conditions for its coupling with the Gaussian free field. We also introduce a framework that allows one to treat all L"owner equations and known types of coupling as different manifestations of the same phenomenon.
item.dc:creator: Alexey Tochin

item.title: Constant solutions of the SU(2) Yang-Mills-Dirac equations: classification and explicit form
item.description:
arXiv:2207.12313v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a complete classification of all constant solutions of the ${m SU}(2)$ Yang--Mills--Dirac equations in Minkowski space ${\mathbb R}^{1,3}$. The method combines the hyperbolic singular value decomposition of the real matrix of the gauge potential with the two-sheeted covering of ${m SO}(3)$ by ${m SU}(2)$. In the degenerate case of zero potential, we classify the solutions by the causal structure of the current. For nondegenerate solutions with $\Psi
eq 0$ and $A
eq 0$, the equations force a sharp dichotomy: a nonzero constant current requires a nonzero mass, and massless solutions necessarily have zero current. The massive branch gives a constant non-Abelian field configuration with nonvanishing invariant $F^2=F_{\mu
u}F^{\mu
u}$. The remaining (degenerate) solutions are classified for completeness. For each case we give explicit formulas for the spinor $\Psi$, the potential $A$, the current $J$, and the invariant $F^2$, and we summarize the classification in a table. Nonconstant solutions can be sought as perturbation-theory series around constant solutions. We write the linear equations for the first-order correction, which reduce to linear partial differential equations with constant coefficients, and find explicit plane-wave solutions of these equations in the massless case.
item.dc:creator: D. S. Shirokov

item.title: Glued tree lattices with only compact localized states
item.description: arXiv:2503.22843v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Flat band physics is a central theme in modern condensed matter physics. By constructing a tight--binding single particle system that has vanishing momentum dispersion in one or more bands, and subsequently including more particles and interactions, it is possible to study physics in strongly interacting regimes. Inspired by the glued trees that first arose in one of the few known examples of quantum supremacy, we define and analyze two infinite families of tight binding single particle Bose--Hubbard models that have only flat bands, and only compact localized states despite having any nonnegative number of translation symmetries. The first class of model that we introduce is constructed by replacing a sufficiently large fraction of the edges in a generic countable graph with glued trees modified to have complex hoppings. The second class arises from thinking of complex weighted glued trees as rhombi that can then be used to tile two dimensional space, giving rise to the familiar dice lattice and infinitely many generalizations thereof, of which some are Euclidian while others are hyperbolic.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Osborne, Ciro Salcedo, Andrew A. Houck

item.title: Solvable Structures for Hamiltonian Systems
item.description: arXiv:2504.02189v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a geometric framework connecting solvable structures and integrable Hamiltonian systems. For a completely integrable Hamiltonian system with $n$ degrees of freedom, we construct a solvable structure consisting of $2n$ Hamiltonian vector fields that allows us to integrate Hamilton's equations by quadratures. Explicit expressions are derived for the associated Pfaffian forms whose integration yields both the solutions of Hamilton's equations and action-angle variables. This provides a novel interpretation of the Arnold-Liouville theorem in the context of solvable structures. We illustrate the theory by deriving explicit solutions and canonical variables of action-angle type for the open Toda lattice and the rational Calogero-Moser system.
item.dc:creator: Sasa Kresic-Juric, Concepcion Muriel, Adrian Ruiz

item.title: Large scale dynamical response of interacting $1d$ Fermi systems
item.description: arXiv:2509.08665v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider the dynamics of a class of weakly interacting, gapless $1d$ fermionic systems, in presence of small external perturbations slowly varying in space and in time. We consider the evolution of the expectation values of the charge density and of the current density, in the thermodynamic limit and for low enough temperatures. We prove the validity and the asymptotic exactness of linear response in the limit of vanishing space-time variation of the perturbation, and we provide the explicit expression of the response of the system. The proof relies on the representation of the real time Duhamel expansion in terms of Euclidean correlation functions, for which we provide sharp estimates using rigorous renormalization group methods. The asymptotic exactness of linear response holds thanks to a cancellation for the scaling limit of the correlations that is reminiscent of bosonization, and which is derived rigorously using emergent chiral Ward identities.
item.dc:creator: Marcello Porta, Giuseppe Scola, Harman Preet Singh

item.title: Effective Dynamics for Weakly Interacting Bosons in an Iterated High-Density Thermodynamic Limit
item.description: arXiv:2510.00839v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the time evolution of weakly interacting Bose gases on a three-dimensional torus of arbitrary volume. The coupling constant is supposed to be inversely proportional to the density, which is considered to be large and independent of the particle number. We take into account a class of initial states exhibiting quasi-complete Bose-Einstein condensation. For each fixed time in a finite interval, we prove the convergence of the one-particle reduced density matrix towards the projection onto the normalised order parameter describing the condensate - evolving according to the Hartree equation - in the iterated limit where the volume (and therefore the particle number), and subsequently the density go to infinity. The rate of convergence depends only on the density and on the decay of both the expected number of particles and the energy of the initial quasi-vacuum state.
item.dc:creator: Daniele Ferretti, Kalle Koskinen

item.title: The Lee-Huang-Yang energy for a dilute gas of hard spheres: an upper bound
item.description: arXiv:2603.13084v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider a quantum gas consisting of $N$ hard spheres with radius $\frak{a} > 0$, obeying bosonic statistics and moving in the box $\Lambda = [0;L]^3$ with periodic boundary conditions. We are interested in the ground state energy per unit volume in the thermodynamic limit, with $N, L \to \infty$ at fixed density $\rho = N / L^3$. We derive an upper bound for the ground state energy density, matching the famous Lee-Huang-Yang formula, up to lower order terms, in the dilute limit $\rho \frak{a}^3 \ll 1$.
item.dc:creator: Giulia Basti, Morris Brooks, Serena Cenatiempo, Alessandro Olgiati, Benjamin Schlein

item.title: Geometry of Critical Couplings, Quartic Binding, and Spectral Shift for Concentric $\delta$-Shells
item.description: arXiv:2603.24028v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the first zero-energy resonance of finitely many attractive concentric spherical $\delta$-shells with fixed radii and variable strengths. The positive critical strengths form a smooth hypersurface in coupling space. For every nonzero tangent redistribution we calculate its second fundamental form as an explicit strictly positive quadratic form $C_a$ in cumulative weighted coupling changes. Along the straight perturbation $g_*+\varepsilon a$, the same coefficient determines the unique emerging bound state, $E_b=-C_a^2\varepsilon^4+O(|\varepsilon|^5)$, for either sign of $\varepsilon$, and the crossover of the canonically normalized total spectral shift on the scale $k\asymp\varepsilon^2$. We also give a global smooth parametrization of the positive critical surface by probability weights, determine the exact attainable interval of effective ranges, and reconstruct all critical strengths from individual threshold-pole responses. An exact coupling coordinate gives a uniform $O(k^3)$ spectral-shift normal form and a differentiated $O(k^2)$ estimate without a restriction on the ratio of coupling distance to wave number. The scattering determinant and general threshold exponents are established inputs. Our results give the model-specific curvature coefficient, its spectral consequences, and a complete local and global description of the first-critical configurations.
item.dc:creator: Masahiro Kaminaga

item.title: Stroboscopic Ergodic Averages and Radial Symmetry in the Vortex Model
item.description: arXiv:2607.00721v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the point-vortex model in the plane in the case of $N$ vortices of equal positive circulation, and we investigate the long-time behaviour of the empirical vorticity measure. We conjecture that, for almost every initial datum, the time average of the empirical measure exists and is invariant under rotations about the centre of vorticity. We prove the conjecture for $N=3$ by exploiting the integrability of the system. For $N\ge 4$ we reduce the problem to a question about a measure-preserving dynamical system on the shape space: after replacing time with a suitably chosen rotation angle as independent variable, radiality is equivalent to the independence of stroboscopic ergodic averages from the initial phase along a single trajectory. We formulate this reduction as a general ergodic problem, discuss its scope through elementary counterexamples, and verify the required hypotheses in explicit regions of the phase space for $N=3$ and $N=4$.
item.dc:creator: Emanuele Caglioti, Marco Cecchini

item.title: On Leray's Theoreme de Structure for a weak solution to the Navier-Stokes equations: an improvement of the result
item.description: arXiv:2607.21380v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this note we furnish a new result concerning the well known th\'eor\`eme de structure by Leray related to a weak solution to the Navier-Stokes equations. We are able to furnish a new estimate on the left endpoint of the unbounded interval of regularity.
item.dc:creator: Paolo Maremonti

item.title: Classification of abstract Bose field models
item.description: arXiv:2609.03863v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We classify a class of abstract Bose field models in quantum field theory up to unitary equivalence. The class includes abstract free Bose field models, abstract van Hove--Miyatake models, and infrared-renormalized van Hove--Miyatake models. Moreover, as an application of our classification, we classify quadratic interaction models. In particular, our results answer a question of A. Arai concerning the classification of infrared-renormalized van Hove--Miyatake models.
item.dc:creator: Yasumichi Matsuzawa

item.title: The phase coordinates transformation in Moyal noncommutative framework 2-dimensional harmonic oscillator and Painlev\'e second equation
item.description: arXiv:2609.08525v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This work aims to explore the physical application of Moyal noncom- mutative formalism with the the presentation of new transformations which connect the old canonical coordinates to purly noncommuting phase coordi- nates through the parameters describe the Moyal noncommutative deforma- tion. These transformations are consistent with the Moyal noncommunica- tive brackets and build sixteen components traceless anti-symmetric tensor. This formalism incorporates space-space and space-momentum noncommu- taivity rather then noncommutativity (Heisenberg quantum commutation ) only for the canonical coordinates. The transformations imply to construct noncommutative analogs of 2-dimensional harmonic oscillator with its superintegrability and Painlev\'e second equation. The associated deformed Hamiltonians additionally involve some extra symmetries and reveal a deep physical understanding of about the additional symmetries with noncommunicative structure. The Painlev\'e second noncommutative coordinates transformation are also efficiently applied to generate the first Yablonskii Vorobev polynomial with Painlev\'e second parameter transformation.
item.dc:creator: Irfan Mahmood

item.title: Differential Recursions, Projective Discriminants, and Algebraic Generating Functions
item.description: arXiv:2609.31189v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Two hierarchies of bivariate generating functions arise from differential recursions with rational initial data: a self-dual hierarchy and a reduced-symmetry hierarchy. At order $p=3$, their rational coefficients yield the triangles OEIS A140136 and A336110, together with a positive palindromic numerator triangle for the odd sector. In general, the reduced hierarchy decomposes into $p-1$ Horn companions, and an explicit differential intertwiner of order $p-3$ relates the last companion to the normalized self-dual series. The Narayana quadratic ($p=2$) and the $S_4$-symmetric Gross--Witten--Wadia quartic ($p=3$, with two tetrahedral edge resolvents) serve as explicit low-order benchmarks. For every $p \ge 3$, we prove that the distinguished reduced generating function has exact algebraic degree $2(p-1)$ over $\mathbb{Q}(x,h^{p-1})$ and that every Horn companion is algebraic. Over $h$, the rational uniformization lifts to the Fermat curve $s^{p-1}+w^{p-1}=1$ of genus $(p-2)(p-3)/2$ with generic monodromy and Galois group $S_{2(p-1)}$. This uniform cover establishes the universal boundary factorization at $H=h^{p-1}=0$ and explains the cubic characteristic factor $\mathcal{A}_p^3$ (carrying a projective $S_3$ action) in the discriminant via $(2,3)$-cusp geometry, illustrated by exact sextic and octic equations and higher-order slices. Conversely, a nonexact differential on the Fermat curve combined with full $S_{2(p-1)}$ monodromy proves that the distinguished self-dual function is transcendental for all $p \ge 4$. The complete factorization of the generic reduced discriminant remains open.
item.dc:creator: S. Voloshyn

item.title: An Egorov-type Theorem for Analytic Wick Observables in Quantum Field Theory
item.description: arXiv:2610.39806v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We provide an exact Egorov-type formula, given by a convergent expansion in the semi-classical parameter $\varepsilon > 0$, for the propagation of a certain class of analytic Wick observables with super-exponentially decaying coefficients, under the action of a time-dependent quadratic Hamiltonian. This work generalizes a result established by S. Breteaux for polynomial symbols, and includes the spatially cutoff $P(\varphi)_2$ model, as well as a variant of the H\"oegh-Krohn model.
item.dc:creator: Julien Malartre

item.title: Concentration of Quasimodes at Spherical Interface between 3D-Topological Insulators
item.description: arXiv:2611.16809v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this work, we study the edge states localized at a spherical interface between two $3\mathrm{D}$-topological insulators from a continuous model of the semiclassical Dirac equation. Using the dynamical and spectral properties of the semiclassical Dirac operator tangent to the interface and the Landau level stratification of the energy in the transverse variable, we describe several concentration and invariance properties of the semiclassical measures associated with quasimodes of the system localized at the interface. Moreover, we construct explicit quasimodes which fulfill some of these properties and concentrate on some particular single periodic geodesics of the sphere.
item.dc:creator: V\'ictor Arnaiz, \'Eric Vacelet

item.title: On the $\phi^4_2$ theory on $\mathbb R\times S$
item.description: arXiv:2611.23032v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a construction of the Euclidean two-dimensional $\phi^4$ quantum field theory model on $\mathbb R\times S$ using parabolic stochastic quantization and discuss the Osterwalder-Schrader axioms. Motivated by one-loop string scattering amplitudes, we first construct finite-volume measures on a family of tori with varying geometry. To construct an infinite-volume measure on the cylinder, we establish uniform renormalization and stochastic estimates as the complex structure varies, including the degenerating regime in which the torus approaches an infinite cylinder.
item.dc:creator: Azam Jahandideh

item.title: Uniformly Expanding Coupled Maps: Self-Consistent Transfer Operators and Propagation of Chaos
item.description: arXiv:2209.13571v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove quantitative propagation of chaos in total variation, uniformly in time, for systems of $N$ deterministic uniformly expanding heterogeneously coupled maps. The local dynamics and interactions may vary between coordinates, so exchangeability is not required. Under assumptions (independent of the dimension) on expansion, regularity, and weak-coupling, we construct self-consistent transfer operators whose product evolutions approximate every fixed finite marginal. For a class of weakly dependent initial laws (containing products), the error is $O(N^{-1})$ on fixed time intervals and $O(\log N/N)$ uniformly in time. The finite-time rate is optimal within this class. An explicit family exhibits error of order $\sqrt{\log N}/N$ at times of order $\log N$, proving that a uniform $O(N^{-1})$ bound is impossible in general; the optimal correction remains open. The proof is based on ergodic theory: expansion preserves classes of regular, weakly dependent densities, while transfer-operator contraction controls error accumulation. These classes yield concentration estimates and allow direct comparison of densities, giving strong propagation of chaos without external noise. Under additional assumptions, we also obtain Gaussian approximation for empirical observables on fixed time intervals and invariant neighbourhoods of stable fixed points of the self-consistent operator.
item.dc:creator: Samuel Ekstroem, Matteo Tanzi, Giuseppe Tenaglia

item.title: A convergence result for a local planning problem for mean field games and rigorous proof of a Freidlin-Ventchel-type Large Deviations Principle for the $1+1$ KPZ equation
item.description: arXiv:2401.02024v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study an innovative connection between a very singular optimal transport variational problem with a congestion term connecting two Dirac measures, which is related to the planing problem in mean field games or gases with negative pressure, and a large deviation principle for the KPZ equation. The main result proves a limit of a singular approixmate problem with vanishing diffusive flux and a relaxed initial condition. The paper also provides a rigorous justification for the informal analysis of the ad hoc large deviation principle for the KPZ equation appearing in the physics literature.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Archive for Rational Mechanics and Analysis (2026)
item.dc:creator: Pierre-Louis Lions, Panagiotis E. Souganidis

item.title: Exact Solutions to the Klein--Gordon Equation via Reduction Algebras
item.description: arXiv:2507.04572v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Reduction algebras (also known as generalized Mickelsson algebras, Zhelobenko algebras, or transvector algebras) are well-studied associative algebras appearing in the representation theory of Lie algebras. In the 1990s, Zhelobenko noted that reduction algebras have a connection to field equations from physics, whereas Howe's study of dual pairs in the 1980s signifies that the link originated even earlier. In this paper, we revisit the simplest case of a massless scalar field, in arbitrary spacetime dimension $n\ge 3$ and arbitrary flat metric $\eta_{ab}$; the field equation then specializes to the Laplace equation and to the massless Klein--Gordon equation. The relevant reduction algebra comes from a representation of $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ (technically, $\mathfrak{sp}_2$) by differential operators. We give a complete presentation of this reduction algebra. Its raising operators produce bosonic states $|a_1a_2\cdots a_\ell\rangle$, polynomial solutions of degree $\ell$ to the field equation, and we show that the natural bilinear form on these states is computed by symmetrizers built from the rational dynamical R-matrix. Along the way we give explicit formulas for the states, and a self-contained proof, for a general metric, of Zhelobenko's results that they span the polynomial solutions and that the solution space is an irreducible module over the reduction algebra.
item.dc:creator: Jonas T. Hartwig, Lillian Ryan Uhl, Dwight Anderson Williams II

item.title: Dirac reduction algebra
item.description: arXiv:2507.21730v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: There is a homomorphism of associative superalgebras from the enveloping algebra of the orthosymplectic Lie superalgebra $\mathfrak{osp}(1|2)$ to the Weyl-Clifford superalgebra $A(2n|n)$ with $2n$ even Weyl algebra generators and $n$ odd Clifford algebra generators. Under this homomorphism, the positive odd root vector $x\in\mathfrak{osp}(1|2)$ is sent to the Dirac operator $\gamma^\mu\partial_\mu\in A(2n|n)$ and generates a left ideal $I$. The corresponding reduction (super)algebra, denoted $Z_n$, is the normalizer of $I$ in $A(2n|n)$ modulo $I$. By construction, $Z_n$ acts on the space of all Clifford algebra-valued polynomial solutions to the (massless) Dirac equation. This setting goes back to Zhelobenko, who described generators of this reduction algebra and commutation relations among them. In this paper, we find a complete presentation of (a localization of) this so-termed Dirac reduction algebra, with full proofs. We give a closed formula for products of the raising operators in the reduction algebra and use it to write down explicitly the polynomial solutions to the Dirac equation in $n$-dimensional flat spacetime that they generate. Finally, we show that for $n\neq 2$ the space of polynomial solutions is irreducible over the reduction algebra tensored with the opposite Clifford algebra when $n$ is even, and is a direct sum of two irreducible submodules when $n$ is odd.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Dorang, Jonas T. Hartwig, Dwight Anderson Williams II

item.title: Kapranov $L_{\infty}[1]$ algebras
item.description: arXiv:2509.26341v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Given any K\"ahler manifold $X$, Kapranov discovered a nontrivial $L_\infty[1]$ algebra structure on $\Omega^{0,\bullet}_{X}(T^{1,0}X)$. Motivated by this result, we introduce the notion of an $L_\infty[1]$ $\mathfrak{R}$-algebra, generalizing $L_\infty[1]$ algebras, where $\mathfrak{R}$ is a differential graded commutative algebra with unit. We extend standard notions such as quasi-isomorphism and linearization to this setting and establish a linearization theorem. As an application, we prove that any DG Lie algebroid $(\mathcal{L},Q_{\mathcal{L}})$ over a DG manifold $(\mathcal{M},Q)$ induces a distinguished isomorphism class of $L_\infty[1]$ $\mathfrak{R}$-algebra structures on $\Gamma(\mathcal{L})$, where $\mathfrak{R}$ is the DG commutative algebra $(C^\infty(\mathcal{M}),Q)$. Their unary bracket is $Q_{\mathcal{L}}$, while their binary bracket is a cocycle representative of the Atiyah class of the DG Lie algebroid. All these isomorphic $L_\infty[1]$ $\mathfrak{R}$-algebra structures are $\mathfrak{R}$-linearizable if and only if the Atiyah class of the DG Lie algebroid vanishes. In contrast, the induced $L_\infty[1]$ $\mathbb{K}$-algebra structures on $\Gamma(\mathcal{L})$ are necessarily $\mathbb{K}$-linearizable, hence $\mathbb{K}$-homotopy abelian.
item.dc:creator: Ruggero Bandiera, Seokbong Seol, Mathieu Sti\'enon, Ping Xu

item.title: Localisation with on-shell supersymmetry algebras via the Batalin-Vilkovisky formalism: Localisation as gauge fixing
item.description: arXiv:2511.01810v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Batalin-Vilkovisky formalism provides a powerful technique to deal with gauge and global (super)symmetries that may only hold on shell. We argue that, since global (super)symmetries and gauge symmetries appear on an equal footing in the Batalin-Vilkovisky formalism, similarly localisation with respect to global (super)symmetries appears on an equal footing with gauge fixing of gauge symmetries; in general, when the gauge-fixing condition is not invariant under the global symmetries, localisation (with respect to a localising fermion) and gauge fixing (with respect to a gauge-fixing fermion) combine into a single operation. Furthermore, this perspective enables supersymmetric localisation using only on-shell supermultiplets, dispensing with auxiliary fields, extending an insight first discovered by Losev and Lysov arXiv:2312.13999. We provide the first examples of on-shell localisation for quantum field theories (together with a companion paper by Arvanitakis arXiv:2511.00144).
item.dc:creator: Leron Borsten, Dimitri Kanakaris, Hyungrok Kim

item.title: What is a minimum work transition in stochastic thermodynamics?
item.description: arXiv:2603.11995v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We reassess the concept of transition at minimum work in classical stochastic finite-time thermodynamics, when the system dynamics is modelled by a diffusion process. We show that a well-posed formulation of the optimal control problem corresponding to the minimization of the mean work done on the system during a finite-time transition necessarily requires taking into account speed limits on control protocols. This fact has major qualitative consequences. First, it permits to discriminate between optimal swift engineered equilibration and transitions at minimum work. Second, it shows that in the limit when speed limits are removed, only transitions specified by generalized Schr\"odinger bridges admit a consistent physical interpretation. To illustrate these points, we focus on the simplest model problem: a levitating particle in a Gaussian moving trap.
item.dc:creator: Paolo Muratore-Ginanneschi, Julia Sanders

item.title: Integrability from Homotopy Algebras
item.description: arXiv:2603.12113v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Homotopy algebraic methods have become increasingly influential in the study of field theories. We consider semi-holomorphic Chern--Simons theory and its relation with the principal chiral model. The semi-classical equivalence of the two theories is expected on general grounds, as the principal chiral model arises by eliminating trivial pairs and gauge fixing. We construct this equivalence explicitly as an off-shell, cyclic quasi-isomorphism between the cyclic $L_\infty$-algebras governing the two theories, and show that it directly encodes the Lax connection. This provides a concrete example for studying integrability of a two-dimensional system through the homotopy algebraic lens.
item.dc:creator: Luigi Alfonsi, Leron Borsten, Mehran Jalali Farahani, Hyungrok Kim, Martin Wolf, Charles Alastair Stephen Young

item.title: Continuity of almost commutative manifolds for the spectral propinquity
item.description: arXiv:2603.19128v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that the canonical metric spectral triples of a fixed compact connected spin manifold depend continuously, for the spectral propinquity, on the Riemannian metric endowed with the $C^1$ topology. This continuity extends to almost commutative spectral triples, allowing the Riemannian metric and the Dirac operator of a fixed finite dimensional factor to vary simultaneously. We also establish continuity for metric spectral triples arising from ergodic actions of compact connected Lie groups as the inner product on the Lie algebra varies. Our proofs use a common continuity criterion involving graph norms and commutator seminorms. As a consequence, eigenvalues in any compact interval whose endpoints avoid the limiting spectrum converge with multiplicity. These results relate classical variations of metric data to the geometry of metric spectral triples.
item.dc:creator: Frederic Latremoliere

item.title: Duality of operator Frobenius algebras and solution of Eisenhart-St\"ackel problem in the non-diagonal case
item.description: arXiv:2604.03195v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study Frobenius algebras of operator fields and introduce a novel notion of duality for them. We show that, under the assumption that the operator fields forming the Frobenius algebra are mutual symmetries, the operator fields in the dual Frobenius algebra are also mutual symmetries. This result allows one to construct new infinite-dimensional integrable systems of hydrodynamic type starting from a given one. As the main application, we solve the long-standing Eisenhart--St\"ackel problem for any Segre characteristic and in arbitrary dimension: namely, we describe all nondegenerate finite-dimensional integrable systems whose integrals are quadratic in momenta such that the corresponding $(1,1)$-tensors commute as operator fields.
item.dc:creator: Alexey V. Bolsinov, Andrey Yu. Konyaev, Vladimir S. Matveev

item.title: Fundamental fields in the deformed $W$-algebras
item.description: arXiv:2604.09471v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a simple Lie algebra. Frenkel and Reshetikhin introduced the deformed $W$-algebra $\mathbf{W}_{qt}(\mathfrak{g})$. In this work, we give a formal version of this definition. In this setting, we reformulate and prove the well-definedness of an algorithm (arxiv:2103.15247, arxiv:2205.08312) inspired by the Frenkel-Mukhin algorithm (arXiv:math/9911112) which, starting from a given dominant monomial $m$ satisfying some degree conditions, produces elements of the deformed $W$-algebra. Then, we apply this algorithm to construct explicitly some specific elements of $\mathbf{W}_{q,t}(\mathfrak{g})$. In particular, we apply this to prove a conjecture of Frenkel and Reshetikhin in arXiv:q-alg/9708006 in types $B_\ell$, $C_\ell$, and for some nodes in other types. This framework opens up new possibilities for studying explicitly fields in the deformed $W$-algebra $\mathbf{W}_{q,t}(\mathfrak{g})$.
item.dc:creator: Hicham Assakaf

item.title: Quasi-Local Celestial Charges and Multipoles
item.description: arXiv:2604.13362v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We extend Penrose's quasi-local mass definition to include higher-spin charges associated with the celestial $Lw_{1+\infty}$ symmetries and relate them to traditional definitions of multipoles. The resulting formulae provide explicit expressions that can be computed on finite 2-surfaces, given a choice of null hypersurface. They yield a geometric definition of celestial symmetries and multipoles in generic spacetimes in terms of higher-valence solutions to the twistor equations. This, in turn, gives rise to natural flux-balance laws along the null hypersurface. We also present a first-principles phase-space derivation of these charges, starting from a twistor space action for self-dual gravity that can be identified with the standard gravitational asymptotic phase space at null infinity, performing a large gauge transformation analysis and using the Penrose transform to connect with the corresponding spacetime expressions. Finally, we formulate the spacetime analysis in the Plebanski gauge and relate the celestial symmetries to the integrability of self-dual gravity in the case of a self-dual background.
item.dc:creator: Adam Kmec, Lionel Mason, Romain Ruzziconi

item.title: Deformed seminorms, anisotropic sectors and Phragm\'en Lindel\"of principles for $\mathcal{R}(p,q)-$\allowbreak difference operators
item.description: arXiv:2605.24010v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the deformed derivative of the $\mathcal{R}(p,q)-$deformed quantum algebras of Hounkonnou and Bukweli Kyemba on spaces of holomorphic functions, with the induced geometry and growth principles. The deformed derivative maps the holomorphic functions on a disc of radius $\rho$ into those on the disc of radius $\rho/\beta$, $\beta$ being the upper limit of the $n-$th roots of the deformed numbers, and this loss of radius is optimal. For two root structure functions the deformed gauge equals $\max\{|z|,1/\phi_{1}\}$, so that deformed discs are Euclidean above a minimal radius; Borel Carath\'eodory and vector valued Cauchy Hadamard theorems follow. On factorial weighted Banach spaces the deformed derivative has norm $1/r$ and spectrum the closed disc of radius $1/r$. A deformed Borel transform identifies these spaces with weighted Wiener algebras, yields the Gelfand theory, and shows that the associated Fr\'echet space is nuclear. We establish logarithmic convexity and subharmonicity results, Phragm\'en Lindel\"of and Lindel\"of principles in the anisotropic sectors of half aperture $\theta\sup_{k}k^{-1}\log[k]$ and in their curved variants, with sharp critical orders, and a rigidity theorem: under Gaussian growth of the deformed factorials, functions of finite deformed exponential type are entire of order zero and cannot be bounded on a ray unless constant. A dominant term principle shows that, for a large dominant root, the deformed exponential and trigonometric functions have only real simple zeros, localized between explicit geometric means of deformed numbers, whereas the deformed exponential series has nonreal zeros when the two roots have sum at most two.
item.dc:creator: Kaw\`eyim Lankpetre, Isiaka Aremua, Joseph D\'esir\'e Bukweli Kyemba

item.title: Propagation of Regularity for Schroedinger Equations with Time Dependent Potentials
item.description: arXiv:2605.27321v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The dynamics of Schr\"odinger equation with time dependent potentials of general time dependence is considered. It is shown that for localized in space potentials, there is propagation of regularity which is uniformly bounded in higher Sobolev norms. Unlike the cases where the solution scatter, and then propagation is proved via a standard bootstrap argument, the solutions considered here have a part that does not scatter, as expected in general. For this we introduce propagation estimates that work directly in (e.g.) $H^2(\mathcal{R}^3).$
item.dc:creator: Avy Soffer

item.title: Existence of the C-type renormalisation two-cycle
item.description: arXiv:2606.06274v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove the existence of the C-type renormalisation two-cycle, helping to establish the universality of the C-type route to chaos in families of non-invertible maps of the plane. Families of two-dimensional non-invertible maps, with at least two parameters and critical points of fold type, exhibit a distinct type of critical scaling, the C-type. An accumulation of parameter values leads to an infinite collection of coexisting attracting cycles of periods $4^n$ or $2\cdot 4^n$. Asymptotically, period quadrupling is accompanied by parameter-space scaling and state-space scaling governed by particular universal constants. Kuznetsov et. al. explained this phenomenon in terms of a stationary orbit of period two of the renormalisation group (RG) transformation for period-doubling. We prove the existence of the corresponding renormalisation two-cycle in a Banach space of analytic maps and gain rigorous bounds on the corresponding universal state space scaling constants. This result provides a further step in proving a series of outstanding conjectures concerning distinct universality classes for period-doubling. It extends the recent results for unidirectionally-coupled maps (the FS-type) to bidirectionally-coupled maps, and generalises the framework from fixed points to periodic orbits of the corresponding renormalisation operators. It also provides a further step in establishing the conjectured picture that the C-type universality class is born from the FS-type class via a period-doubling bifurcation in the dynamics of the RG transformation itself. The proof relies on rigorous computations to establish that a variant of Newton's method for the two-cycle is a contraction map. The C-type scaling regularity is known to occur in a number of dynamical systems of interest, perhaps most notably in biologically-plausible models of nephron blood pressure autoregulation.
item.dc:creator: Zainab Rahman, Maria Pickett, Andrew Burbanks

item.title: Entropic Uncertainty Relations for Mutually Unbiased Operator Frames
item.description: arXiv:2606.23185v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop an operator-frame formulation of entropic uncertainty relations in the Hilbert-Schmidt space of operators. For general continuous indexed operator frames, we derive an entropic uncertainty relation for the associated coefficient distributions by combining endpoint norm estimates with Riesz-Thorin interpolation. We then identify a distinguished class of mutually unbiased operator frames, defined through constant-modulus trace overlaps. Under suitable structural conditions, the corresponding coefficient amplitudes are related by a bilinear Fourier transform, leading to a stronger Hirschman-Beckner-type entropic uncertainty relation. As canonical realizations, we consider Weyl displacement operators and Wigner kernels, as well as Cartesian dyadic frames generated by position and momentum eigenstates. These examples recover familiar continuous-variable Fourier dualities while extending entropic uncertainty relations beyond measurement outcomes to operator representations themselves.
item.dc:creator: Jesni Shamsul Shaari, Stefano Mancini

item.title: Propagation of chaos for Belavkin equations beyond pure states
item.description: arXiv:2606.29557v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We establish quantitative trace-norm propagation of chaos for finite-dimensional quantum mean-field systems governed by Belavkin equations under continuous diffusive measurements. Our results concern random reduced states conditioned on the observation records of the entire particle system, rather than states averaged over these records. We allow arbitrary one-particle density matrices, general measurement operators, and both perfect and inefficient detection. Two regimes of initial data are considered. For initial states approaching a tensor product in trace norm, without requiring permutation invariance, we establish explicit convergence rates, improved from an inverse fourth-root to an inverse square-root rate when the one-particle initial state is faithful. More importantly, for permutation-invariant initial states, convergence of the two-particle marginal to a product suffices for propagation of chaos, even when the full initial state remains far from a tensor product. Quantitative convergence rates are obtained in this setting, including a sharper estimate under faithfulness. Our proofs combine purification, fully observed dilation, and uniform stability of linear Zakai equations with a relative-entropy method for the joint observation law and conditional quantum state. The latter controls the interacting dynamics through entropy-production estimates and extends to arbitrary-rank initial states by regularizing only the reference dynamics. These results provide a rigorous foundation for low-dimensional approximations of continuously monitored interacting quantum systems, including those with initially correlated states.
item.dc:creator: Gaoyue Guo

item.title: Penalized hyperviscous Navier-Stokes flows: well-posedness, incompressible limit and sharp decay
item.description: arXiv:2607.10657v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study a three-dimensional Navier--Stokes system obtained by Temam's penalty method in the presence of a biharmonic viscosity: the pressure and the divergence constraint are replaced by the term $-\varepsilon^{-1}\nabla\,div\,u$, and the convection term is written in skew-symmetric form. We prove global well-posedness in $L^2(\mathbb{R}^3)$ and global regularity for data of arbitrary size in $H^2(\mathbb{R}^3)$, with bounds uniform in $\varepsilon$ and in time. For data in $L^1\cap L^2$, the energy decays like $t^{-3/2}$, with a constant independent of $\varepsilon$; for data in $L^1\cap H^2$, the first two derivatives decay at the corresponding heat rates. We identify the leading asymptotic profile and show that $t^{3/2}\|u(t)\|_{L^2}^2\to\gamma_\varepsilon(8\pi\nu)^{-3/2}|m_\infty|^2$, where $m_\infty$ is an asymptotic momentum and the explicit factor $\gamma_\varepsilon\in(\frac23,1)$ measures the energy removed by the penalization. Consequently, the decay rates are optimal in $L^1\cap H^2$ under an explicit non-degeneracy condition. Finally, as $\varepsilon\to0$, the solutions converge globally in time to those of the incompressible hyperviscous Navier--Stokes equations at the rate $\sqrt\varepsilon$, up to an explicit initial layer, and $-\varepsilon^{-1}div\,u$ converges to the pressure.

item.title: Spin-coherent quantum designs
item.description: arXiv:2608.11310v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Coherent states bridge the gap between quantum and classical physics, but their overcomplete and nonorthogonal nature makes it difficult to identify finite sets that represent spin observables exactly. Finite spin-coherent tomography and discrete coherent-state operator bases already exist. Here we address a more specific problem: preserving the canonical contravariant-symbol representation. For a spin-$J$ system, the canonical finite coherent-state formula reconstructs every operator in the rank-$S$ irreducible tensor sector exactly if and only if the sampling directions form a spherical $(2J+S)$-design and the corresponding coherent-state projectors then form a spin-coherent quantum design. We also give an explicit Gauss-Legendre construction which leads to weighted spherical designs. These results provide a systematic way to determine spin-operator moments from finite coherent-state POVMs without full state tomography, with practical protocols for polarimetry and magnetometry. Presented construction can be extended to other compact symmetry groups.
item.dc:creator: Marcin Rudzi\'nski, Aaron Z. Goldberg, Andrei B. Klimov, Luis L. S\'{a}nchez-Soto, Karol \.Zyczkowski

item.title: False-vacuum bubbles in sphaleron scattering
item.description: arXiv:2608.11370v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate the collision dynamics of two bright sphalerons in a (1+1)-dimensional deformed $\phi^6$ scalar field theory with a symmetric potential possessing false vacua. Two one-parameter realizations of the model, referred to as the barrier and well models, are considered and their static and linear instability properties are first reviewed. We then study head-on collisions of boosted sphalerons over a broad range of initial velocities and deformation parameters. The scattering dynamics exhibit a rich variety of final states, including the production of kink-antikink pairs, long-lived oscillons in true and false vacuum, multiple oscillons propagating in false-vacuum regions, and radiative decay. A particularly remarkable outcome is the emergence of a long-lived bubble of the false broken vacuum bounded by a kink-antikink pair, which repeatedly collapses and re-expands before eventually decaying into an oscillon. These results demonstrate that deformed $\phi^6$ theories with false vacua exhibit considerably richer sphaleron dynamics than previously known and provide new insight into the role of unstable localized configurations in nonlinear field theories.
item.dc:creator: Manuel A. Mart\'inez S\'anchez, Christoph Adam, Danial Saadatmand

item.title: Analytic Brill wave initial data with trapped surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.16773v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Since Brill's work of 1959, the conformal factor of finite-amplitude Brill waves, the axisymmetric and time-symmetric vacuum initial data on $\mathbb{R}^3$ that describe pure gravitational radiation, has been obtained only numerically, up to the most recent studies. Here an explicit one-parameter family of such data is constructed; the data are real analytic and asymptotically flat, with trivial topology and a single end. The free metric function is a closed-form combination of elementary functions and a dilogarithm. The data have the toroidal conformal symmetry of Beig and Husa, and a change of variable of Natanzon type reduces every mode equation to the Gauss hypergeometric equation, so that the conformal factor is a series with explicit Gamma-function coefficients. A ground-state identity gives a sharp existence criterion: complete, asymptotically flat data exist precisely for $k<k_c=0.80480168\ldots$, and the explicit series is identified with the unique variational solution. The ADM mass is an absolutely convergent digamma series, with $m/a=\pi k^2/10+O(k^3)$ for small amplitudes and an explicit residue at its critical divergence. Sufficiently strong waves contain trapped surfaces: it is proved that for $k$ close to $k_c$ the rescaled conformal factor converges to an explicit function and explicit tori and spheres become outer trapped, so that the data contain an apparent horizon. A numerical search, restricted to equatorially symmetric star-shaped surfaces, finds marginally trapped (minimal) spheres, which appear in a fold near $k=0.7670$. A scaling symmetry of the mode problem generates further solvable families, whose simplest member has the elementary seed function $q=\frac12\log[1+4a^2\rho^2/(\rho^2+z^2+a^2)^2]$. No thin-torus or weak-field approximation is used.
